title: Bounded augmented truncation at an injective final kernel
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $N$ an $R$-module, in a common universe. Let $I^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex, zero in negative degrees, with injective terms, and let $\varepsilon:N\to I^0$ make $0\to N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\xrightarrow{\partial^0}I^1\to\cdots$ exact [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix an integer $d\geq0$ and suppose that $J=\ker(\partial^d:I^d\to I^{d+1})$ is injective. Define the graded modules $L^j=I^j$ for $0\leq j<d$, $L^d=J$, and $L^j=0$ otherwise. There are differentials making $L^\bullet$ a cochain complex, equal to $\partial^j$ for $0\leq j<d-1$ and equal to the corestriction $I^{d-1}\to J$ of $\partial^{d-1}$ when $d>0$, all remaining differentials being zero. There is a chain map $\lambda:L^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ which is the identity in degrees $0\leq j<d$, the inclusion $J\hookrightarrow I^d$ in degree $d$, and zero in other degrees, and an augmentation $e:N[0]\to L^\bullet$ satisfying $\lambda e=\varepsilon$. Here $e^0=\varepsilon$ if $d>0$, while for $d=0$ it is the induced isomorphism $N\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. The augmentation $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $L^\bullet$ is injective, and $L^j=0$ outside $[0,d]$. In particular $e$ induces an isomorphism $N[0]\cong L^\bullet$ in the derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For $d>0$, define $\delta^{d-1}(x)=\partial^{d-1}(x)$ regarded as an element of $J$. This is well-defined since $\partial^d\partial^{d-1}(x)=0$, and is $R$-linear because $J$ is a submodule. Use the prescribed retained differentials and zero elsewhere. Consecutive retained maps compose to zero; at $j=d-2$ the composite is $\partial^{d-1}\partial^{d-2}=0$ with codomain restricted to $J$. Every other composite involving a zero map is zero. For $d=0$ all maps are zero. Thus $\delta^2=0$ in every case.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: Define $\lambda^j$ by the stated identities, inclusion, and zero maps. For $0\le j<d-1$ its chain-map equation is an identity. At $j=d-1$ it is the defining equation for the corestriction. At $j=d$ it says $\partial^d|_J=0$, true by the definition of $J$. At every other $j$ both sides vanish. When $d=0$, the same kernel identity handles degree zero and the other equations are zero. Hence $\lambda$ is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: Exactness of the given augmented sequence says that $\varepsilon$ is injective and $\operatorname{im}\varepsilon=\ker\partial^0$. If $d>0$, set $e^0=\varepsilon$ and $e^j=0$ for $j\ne0$. For $d>1$ the equation $\delta^0e^0=0$ is $\partial^0\varepsilon=0$; for $d=1$ it is the same equation corestricted to $J$. Thus $e:N[0]\to L$ is a chain map. If $d=0$, corestrict $\varepsilon$ to $J=\ker\partial^0$: it is injective and surjective by the preceding equalities, so is the asserted $R$-linear isomorphism. It also defines a chain map. Degreewise, $\lambda e=\varepsilon$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: Assume $d>0$. For $0<j<d-1$, $\ker\delta^j=\ker\partial^j$ and $\operatorname{im}\delta^{j-1}=\operatorname{im}\partial^{j-1}$, so $H^j(L)=0$ by exactness of the given sequence. If $d>1$, the same holds at $j=d-1$, since corestricting a map to a submodule of its codomain does not change its kernel: an element maps to zero there exactly when its image in the original codomain is zero. At $j=d$, $\ker\delta^d=J$ and $\operatorname{im}\delta^{d-1}=J$ by exactness at $I^d$, so $H^d(L)=J/J=0$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: For $d>0$, the degree-zero incoming differential is zero and $\ker\delta^0=\ker\partial^0=\operatorname{im}\varepsilon$; when $d=1$, the kernel equality again uses the inclusion $J\hookrightarrow I^1$. Hence $H^0(e)$ is an isomorphism, using injectivity of $\varepsilon$. Outside $[0,d]$ the terms, and therefore cohomology, vanish. Together with the preceding step this proves $e$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $d=0$, $L=J[0]$ and the isomorphism $e^0$ already gives this conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: For $0\le j<d$, $L^j=I^j$ is injective by hypothesis; $L^d=J$ is injective by hypothesis. Every remaining term is zero. The zero module is injective directly from the extension definition: a map $M\to0$ is zero and extends along any monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow P$ by the zero map $P\to0$. Thus all terms are injective and the stated support is $[0,d]$, also when $d=0$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1): the complex ending in J; explicit module-level verification of that truncation.

proof.text: By the localization definition of $D(R)$, the quasi-isomorphism $e$ is inverted by $Q$, so $Q(e):N[0]\to Q(L)$ is an isomorphism. This is the claimed derived-category isomorphism induced by the prescribed augmentation.

lean.statement: theorem exists_injective_final_kernel_truncation {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (hneg : ∀ j : ℤ, j < 0 → IsZero (I.X j)) (hinj : ∀ j : ℤ, Injective (I.X j)) (ε : (single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj N ⟶ I) [QuasiIso ε] (d : ℤ) (hd : 0 ≤ d) (hJ : Injective (kernel (I.d d (d + 1)))) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)] : ∃ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (ι : L ⟶ I) (e : (single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj N ⟶ L) (a : ∀ (j : ℤ), 0 ≤ j → j < d → (L.X j ≅ I.X j)) (b : L.X d ≅ kernel (I.d d (d + 1))), (∀ (j : ℤ) (hj : 0 ≤ j) (hjd : j < d), ι.f j = (a j hj hjd).hom) ∧ ι.f d = b.hom ≫ kernel.ι (I.d d (d + 1)) ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, j < 0 ∨ d < j → IsZero (L.X j) ∧ ι.f j = 0) ∧ (∀ (i j : ℤ) (hi : 0 ≤ i) (hid : i < d) (hj : 0 ≤ j) (hjd : j < d), j = i + 1 → L.d i j ≫ (a j hj hjd).hom = (a i hi hid).hom ≫ I.d i j) ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ) (hi : 0 ≤ i) (hid : i < d), i + 1 = d → L.d i d ≫ b.hom ≫ kernel.ι (I.d d (d + 1)) = (a i hi hid).hom ≫ I.d i d) ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, ¬ (0 ≤ j ∧ j < d) → L.d j (j + 1) = 0) ∧ e ≫ ι = ε ∧ (∀ hpos : 0 < d, e.f 0 ≫ (a 0 (le_refl 0) hpos).hom = ε.f 0) ∧ (d = 0 → IsIso (e.f 0)) ∧ QuasiIso e ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, Injective (L.X j)) ∧ ∃ η : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((single (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj N) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L, η.hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map e
